courses.title: Consecutive Interpreting: Cantonese-English
courses.description: This course provides intensive training on consecutive interpreting techniques between Cantonese and English, which include short-term memory training, active listening, paraphrasing, note-taking and message reconstitution. Students will also learn to manage psychological demands in high-stakes settings (e.g., legal, medical, or domestic crises) while maintaining professional distance and stable performance.

courses.subject: TRAN
courses.title: Post-editing Machine Translation
courses.description:
The class will feature a general introduction to machine/AI translation, alongside discussions on the philosophy behind post-editing translations (what is the relationship between the human and the machine?) and a focus on productivity (how can we make best use of our time?). While practical training in pre-editing and post-editing techniques between Chinese and English will be offered, including edit distance and the level of edit to apply (light or heavy), the core of the course will be detailed discussions and practice aimed at discovering how to increase productivity in producing postedited output. The course will prepare students with the understanding and skills necessary to engage in professional post-editing tasks, to improve their own individual workflows, and to face a future where all translation work involves the manipulation of AI generated text.

The course is taught in English and Chinese, with both English and Chinese materials.
courses.learning_outcomes:
• Have a better understanding of the principles of machine translation

• Ability to use a number of different machine translation engines and evaluate their output

• Ability to post-edit texts that have been translated by machine translation engines and apply the required level of edit

• Ability to meet specific requirements based on text-type and other contexts during post-editing tasks

• Ability to manage large-scale machine translation and post-editing projects

• Understand the importance of the role played by machine translation and post-editing in the global translation industry
courses.course_syllabus:
Understanding the machine

* A simple and mostly non-technical look at how machine translation operates, from statistical machine translation to neural machine translation and beyond, into the realm of LLMs and Transformer models. The various pros and cons of machine translation will be considered, alongside discussion of which text types are most suitable for MT and what kinds of common mistakes the post-editor should look out for.

Pre-editing

* The pre-editing of machine translation involves preparing a text for translation by following certain stylistic or terminological guidelines in an effort to improve the quality of the output.

Light and heavy post-editing

* Post-editing techniques such as “light” post-editing (making a text understandable) and “heavy” post-editing (increasing quality to a publishable standard) will be discussed and practiced

Edit distance

* A way of showing how much effort is required to edit a machine translation: that is, how many steps does it take to correct a mistake?

Productivity

* Using keylogging and screen capture software to record editing sessions and understand the mechanics of the process, self-reflection on editing practice.

Collaborative post-editing

* Students will be expected to complete a group project that requires working as a team on a large translation project.

courses.subject: TRAN
courses.title: Translation Technologies in the Age of AI
courses.description:
This course trains students on the use of fully automatic and/or interactive translation systems in the age of AI.

The course is taught in English and Putonghua, with teaching materials in Chinese and English.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students will be able to:

* **Understand** the basic of using programme languages as a tool in translation process.**Utilize** programming languages to automate essential text processing tasks, including file handling, data structuring, and natural language processing (using libraries such as NLTK and Jieba).
* **Implement** automated translation workflows by connecting to external Machine Translation and Generative AI services (e.g., Google Translate, Baidu, OpenAI) via Application Programming Interfaces (APIs).
* **Apply** computational metrics (such as BLEU and COMET) and data visualization techniques to evaluate and compare the quality of MT- and/or AI-generated translations scientifically.
* **Design** and execute practical projects that leverage coding skills to perform bulk translation, bilingual corpus analysis, or translation quality assessment.
courses.course_syllabus:
Core Python Skills

* Variables and Data Types
* Conditional statements (if, elif, else)
* Loops and Iterations (for, while)
* Defining and calling functions
* Modules and importing libraries

File Management

* Reading from and writing to files
* Handling translation formats (txt, csv, json)

Natural Language Processing (NLP)

* String manipulation and Regular Expressions (Regex)
* Tokenization and Normalization
* English processing: NLTK / SpaCy
* Chinese segmentation: Jieba

Understanding APIs (Application Programming Interfaces)

* Request/Response cycles
* Handling API keys and authentication

Integration with MT & AI Services

* Connecting to Google Translate / Baidu Translate
* Connecting to Large Language Models (e.g., OpenAI/ChatGPT)
* Batch processing: Automating bulk translation of documents

Automatic Evaluation Metrics

* n-gram based metrics: BLEU
* Neural-based metrics: COMET

Comparative Analysis

* Comparing output from different engines (e.g., NMT vs. LLM)
* Reference-based vs. Reference-free evaluation

Visualizing Translation Data

* Introduction to plotting libraries (e.g., Matplotlib, Seaborn)
* Creating charts to compare model performance
* Presenting data-driven insights for translation quality

courses.description: This course introduces students to some of the central issues and basic concepts involved in the study of society and human relationships, in order to help students develop critical thinking and strategies for translating texts that engage with these issues and concepts. 4. Modality (meanings expressed by (but not limited to) modal verbs) in social science texts and the concept of ‘hedging’ 社會科學文本的情態表達及 ‘含糊言语’ 的使用

courses.description:
This course provides an overview of the translation and interpretation (T&I) industry in the local and international contexts. A range of theoretical approaches will be introduced to help students conceptualise the industry and their prospective role in it. They can understand the importance of professional ethics, and be empowered as reflective professionals. They will become familiar with the typical professional practices in both the private and public sectors, including commercial language service companies, and translation departments in official organizations.

The course is taught in both Cantonese and English, with English materials. It is offered for major or minor students.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students are expected to:

* Understand key aspects of the translation sector, with a particular focus on the impact of technology on translation activities and the profession.
* Be familiar with the aspects of professional translation practices, including translation project management, translation, revision and post-editing.
* Recognize and develop their own professional and personal strengths, and enhance their employability by practising a variety of roles that are likely to encounter in professional practice.
* Be able to use specialist translation project management software to organize projects.
* Communicate effectively with clients, translation companies, translation project managers and fellow translators.

* The translation profession; quality assurance; ethics, and codes of practice
* The translation industry in Hong Kong and abroad; translation & interpreting jobs and clients
* Career-starting and career-management skills for the T&I professions
* Working at an agency and project managing; freelancing
* Translation revising and editing
* Professional roles, and society (e.g., translation policy, professional image, language learning)

courses.subject: TRAN
courses.title: Readings in Translated Works
courses.description: This course comprises critical studies of Chinese translations of English writings and English translations of Chinese writings, covering chiefly literary classics of various genres and from different periods. The approach is cultural as well as linguistic, and the aim is not only to introduce the skills and the art of translating, but also to help students appreciate the stylistic considerations and philosophic attitudes involved. Apart from presenting a written paper, students are also expected to actively take part in the oral commentary and analysis of selected works.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Translation or MA Translation
courses.course_syllabus:
The course engages students in practicing a variety of skills, including:

* reading contextually, i.e. an expression may be used differently in different contexts to construct different meanings
* exploring interpretive possibilities, i.e. a text may yield multiple or conflicting meanings
* assessing the options preferred by a translator against the background of rejected options
* examining how a translation can enrich a source text by uncovering unnoticed layers of meaning
* presenting effective arguments in the form of a critical essay or oral commentary

6. 以日為師：維新運動至辛亥革命時期的翻譯活動
7. 翻譯與五四運動
8. 民國時期的名著翻譯時代
9. 抗戰時期的翻譯與抗戰文化
10. 政治與翻譯
11. 翻譯史的外部研究和內部研究

courses.subject: TRAN
courses.title: Translation as Data: Methods, Tools, and Insights
courses.description: This course introduces computational and digital humanities approaches to studying translation between Chinese and English. It begins with a simple idea: translation can be seen as data. The large language models widely used today grew out of research on translation, as the transformer architecture was originally developed for neural machine translation. Because these models now shape how language and meaning are processed on a massive scale, understanding translation in the age of big data is more important than ever. Students will explore translated texts, bibliographic records, and other cultural data using accessible digital tools, with an emphasis on creativity, critical reflection, and the ability to tell new stories about translation and its circulation across cultures.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
For students in MA Translation, or
For students in MPhil Translation
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students will be able to:

1. Identify and curate translation-related datasets (parallel corpora, bibliographic metadata, paratexts, reviews) using basic data management tools (Excel/CSV, bibliographic platforms).
2. Apply text analysis tools (Voyant, AntConc, simple sentiment platforms) to examine word frequencies, concordances, and emotional patterns in Chinese–English translation.

3. Conduct topic and style analysis with accessible methods (e.g., topic modeling via web platforms, stylometry tools) to explore translator style and thematic patterns.
4. Visualize translation flows and networks using Gephi and Tableau/Plotly to map authors, translators, publishers, and circulation routes.
5. Critically assess data-driven approaches to translation studies, with attention to cultural, gender, and social bias, representation, and the limits of computational methods.
6. Design and present an independent project that combines translation studies with one or more data-analytic methods, integrating hands-on practice with critical interpretation.
courses.course_syllabus:
Translation as Data

* Translation as data: texts, bibliographic records, paratexts, reception
* Cultural data analytics in Chinese–English translation
* AI and the rethinking of translation studies

Analyzing Translated Texts and Paratexts

* Corpus-based approaches: keywords, concordance, collocation
* Sentiment and reception: reviews, paratexts, emotional transfer
* Application of topic modeling and stylometry to translator style and thematic patterns

Metadata, Networks, and Circulation

* Bibliographic data in translation studies
* Translation flows between Chinese and English
* Network Visualization (Gephi/Tableau)

Storytelling, Creativity

* Visual storytelling: data transformation into cultural insights
* Student project: integration of analytical tools with critical translation interpretation

courses.subject: TRAN
courses.title: Research Seminar in Translation II
courses.description: This course provides a further forum for research students in translation to develop the ability to explore research topics independently, carry out researches effectively, and manage research resources appropriately. (Pre-requisite: TRAN6910 or approval of instructor)
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Translation or PhD Translation; Prerequisite: TRAN6910
courses.course_syllabus: Students are required to take turn to present 30 minutes, followed by two commentaries (15 min. each) and discussion (about 30 min.)
courses.feedback_evaluation:
Feedback on assignments or comments on performance in any written or verbal format:

* Written comments on students’ works
* Email/Blackboard
* Face to face discussion
courses.required_readings: Since each student’s project is different and therefore the methodology will vary, there is no required reading for this course.
